findings.reason: src/constructFrom/index.ts:53 now reads `typeof date === "object" && constructFromSymbol in date`. Because typeof null is "object", a null date reaches the `in` operator, which throws a TypeError. Before the change, `date &&` skipped this branch and the code fell through to `new Date(value)` at line 59. I kept severity high because this is a public helper and JS callers can pass null.
findings.claim: Removing the `date &&` guard makes constructFrom(null, value) throw a TypeError instead of returning new Date(value).
findings.evidence: The diff changes `if (date && typeof date === "object" && constructFromSymbol in date)` to `if (typeof date === "object" && constructFromSymbol in date)`. Because `typeof null === "object"`, a null `date` now reaches `constructFromSymbol in date`, and the `in` operator throws when its right-hand side is null. Callers that pass a possibly-null reference straight in, such as `parse` calling `constructFrom(options?.in || referenceDate, NaN)` with a null `referenceDate` from JS callers, now crash instead of producing a date.

findings.reason: The diff only deletes `date &&` and adds no test. A grep for `null` in src/constructFrom/ finds no matches, so no test covers this path. The regression itself is already covered by the C1/X1 item, and the packet has no story.md, so I can't confirm the guard removal was unrequested. Severity lowered to low.
findings.claim: The change weakens input validation without being asked to and adds no test for a null reference date.
findings.evidence: The whole diff is the one-line removal of `date &&` in `constructFrom`. A grep for `null` in `src/constructFrom/` finds nothing, and `acceptance.md` names no criterion that calls for changing this guard.
